summary: Usage CSV export could interpret session labels as formulas
description:
### Summary

Usage CSV export could interpret session labels as formulas. In affected versions, the Control UI quoted session labels as CSV text but did not neutralize leading characters that spreadsheet applications can interpret as formulas.

This advisory is scoped to the exported artifact and the spreadsheet application used to open it. OpenClaw did not evaluate the formula itself, and impact required an operator to open the export in software with formula evaluation enabled.

### Impact

A lower-trust participant who influenced a session label or first user message could place a formula-like cell in the Usage export. Opening that file in an affected spreadsheet could evaluate the cell with the spreadsheet user's permissions. Practical impact depended on spreadsheet security settings and formula support.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, import Usage exports as plain text or inspect formula-leading cells before opening them in a spreadsheet.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

summary: Active Memory global toggles could omit owner checks
description:
### Summary

Active Memory global toggles could omit owner checks. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner external-channel sender could enable or disable Active Memory for the Gateway.

This advisory is scoped to persistent global `on` and `off` mutations. Session-level controls and read-only status remain governed by their existing command policy, and OpenClaw does not treat one shared Gateway as adversarial multi-tenant isolation.

### Impact

A non-owner sender could disable memory recall for future sessions or re-enable global recall where the owner expected it to remain disabled. Practical confidentiality and availability impact depends on stored memories and subsequent conversations.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable global Active Memory commands in external channels or restrict command access to owners.

summary: Twilio pre-auth limits could lock out valid webhooks
description:
### Summary

Twilio pre-auth limits could lock out valid webhooks. In affected versions, the SMS webhook applied its invalid-request rate limit before signature verification and identified clients only by the raw proxy socket address.

### Affected configurations

This affected SMS/Twilio webhooks behind a trusted reverse proxy or tunnel where multiple external clients shared one socket address at OpenClaw.

### Impact

An unauthenticated sender could consume the shared pre-auth budget with invalid requests and cause later correctly signed Twilio callbacks to receive HTTP 429. The attacker could not forge a callback or access message data; impact was temporary inbound SMS loss while the shared window remained exhausted.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid placing untrusted traffic and Twilio callbacks behind the same proxy source address, or enforce per-client limits at the proxy.

summary: Discord asset uploads could skip sender media policy
description:
### Summary

Discord emoji and sticker upload actions could lose the sender-scoped media policy before loading a local file. A sender permitted to invoke those actions could cause OpenClaw to read a host path that the same sender's configured media roots would otherwise reject.

### Impact

Affected Discord deployments could place bytes from an out-of-policy local file into an outbound emoji or sticker upload. Exploitation requires access to the guild asset action and knowledge or derivation of a useful local path. The issue did not provide unrestricted filesystem browsing or code execution.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.9.3`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `@openclaw/discord` to `2026.9.3` or later. Until upgraded, deny Discord emoji and sticker upload actions to lower-trust senders and keep their media roots limited to directories that contain no sensitive files.

summary: MCP configuration changes could omit owner authorization
description:
### Summary

MCP configuration changes could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner external-channel sender could use `/mcp set` or `/mcp unset` to persist Gateway MCP server configuration.

This advisory is scoped to mutating MCP chat commands. Installed and owner-configured MCP servers remain trusted integrations; the failed boundary is authorization to add, replace, or remove their process configuration.

### Impact

A non-owner sender could persist an attacker-selected stdio MCP command that executed with the OpenClaw process user's privileges when MCP configuration loaded. This could affect host confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable MCP chat commands in external channels and inspect configured MCP servers for unexpected entries.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

summary: Codex native tools could ignore per-chat policy
description:
### Summary

Codex native tools could ignore per-chat policy. In affected versions, a conversation-level `tools.allow` rule filtered OpenClaw tools but did not restrict shell, process, file, and patch tools owned by the Codex app-server runtime.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When a lower-trust conversation was assigned to a Codex runtime and restricted with a per-chat tool allowlist, a participant who could trigger that agent could still reach native command and file tools. Practical impact depended on the runtime's host permissions and sandbox configuration.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, route restricted chats to an agent runtime without native host tools or disable those tools at the agent boundary.

summary: Active Memory recall could ignore requester policy
description:
### Summary

Active Memory automatic recall could omit the originating requester's effective tool policy. Deterministic and hidden recall paths could retrieve and inject durable memory even when `toolsBySender` explicitly denied that requester access to memory tools.

### Impact

In deployments using Active Memory and requester-specific tool rules, an admitted sender denied `memory_search` and `memory_get` could receive information derived from durable memory in the agent's response. The issue was a deterministic policy omission in context assembly and did not depend on the sender directly invoking a hidden tool.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable Active Memory for conversations containing requesters who are denied memory access, or isolate those conversations in an agent and workspace without sensitive durable memory.

summary: Outbound attachments could ignore requester read denials
description:
### Summary

Outbound attachment handling could read a local path without applying the originating sender's global or per-agent `toolsBySender` policy. A sender explicitly denied filesystem reads could still cause a known host file to be returned through a final-response media directive or message attachment.

### Impact

Affected deployments could disclose local file contents to an admitted requester whose normal agent turn did not include the `read` tool. Exploitation required knowledge or derivation of a useful path and a delivery flow that accepted local attachments.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable local outbound attachments for agents serving restricted senders, keep generated artifacts in dedicated non-sensitive directories, and avoid treating `toolsBySender` read denial alone as an attachment boundary.

summary: OpenAI-compatible transport could send provider credentials to the wrong endpoint
description:
### Summary

OpenAI-compatible transport could send provider credentials to the wrong endpoint. In affected versions, a pinned third-party provider session whose model metadata lacked a concrete base URL could retain that provider's credential while the OpenAI SDK selected its default endpoint after a model hot reload.

### Affected configurations

This affects configurations where a third-party provider uses an OpenAI-compatible API, the resolved model lacks an explicit provider endpoint, and an existing pinned session continues after model configuration is reloaded.

### Impact

A request could disclose the configured third-party provider credential to an unrelated provider endpoint and fail with a misleading authentication error. Operators who observed this condition should rotate the affected credential.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, configure explicit base URLs for third-party OpenAI-compatible providers and avoid continuing pinned sessions after changing model defaults.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: Slack file downloads could miss conversation authorization
description:
### Summary

Slack `download-file` authorization could fail open when a file lacked the share metadata used to prove that it belonged to the requested conversation. A caller limited to one conversation could retrieve a known file outside that scope when the expected relationship data was absent.

### Impact

Affected Slack deployments could disclose file contents across configured conversation boundaries to an authenticated caller who knew or obtained the file identifier. The issue did not permit listing arbitrary Slack files and did not bypass Slack authentication itself.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `@openclaw/slack` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, deny `download-file` to lower-trust senders and avoid relying on conversation scoping for files whose Slack metadata is missing, incomplete, or imported from older records.

summary: Prometheus diagnostics could omit operator.read enforcement
description:
### Summary

The OpenClaw Prometheus diagnostics plugin did not enforce `operator.read` for its authenticated metrics endpoint. An identity-bearing Gateway caller whose effective role had no read scope could retrieve the diagnostics document even though ordinary read methods rejected the same identity.

### Impact

Deployments using the Prometheus plugin with trusted-proxy or another identity-bearing authentication mode could expose operational metrics to an authenticated profile that was intentionally limited below read access. Shared-secret Gateway callers already have the documented full operator scope set and do not create this condition.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.9.3`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade the `@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus` plugin to `2026.9.3` or later. Until upgraded, disable the Prometheus endpoint or ensure every identity allowed to reach it is intended to hold `operator.read`.

summary: Inbound voice calls could inherit owner tool authority
description:
### Summary

Classic inbound voice calls could launch the configured agent without carrying the caller's identity or non-owner status. Owner-only filtering could therefore fail open and expose the agent's normal tool authority to an admitted remote caller.

### Impact

A caller who passed the configured inbound-call policy could steer tools intended for the trusted owner, potentially reading data, modifying files, executing commands, or controlling connected services according to the agent's configuration. Inbound calling had to be enabled, and the caller still had to pass its open, pairing, or allowlist admission policy.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `@openclaw/voice-call` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable classic inbound calling or assign inbound calls to an agent with a strict read-only tool policy and no owner-only capabilities.

summary: QQBot voice filenames could escape the staging directory
description:
### Summary

QQBot voice filenames could escape the staging directory. In affected versions, voice attachment filenames were decoded twice, allowing encoded traversal segments to reappear after filename sanitization.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When a remote QQ sender supplied an attachment that the agent forwarded as voice, attacker-supplied bytes could be written outside the intended voice staging directory to another process-writable location. Generated filename material limited targeted overwrite, but the staging path boundary was not enforced.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable QQBot voice forwarding for lower-trust senders and remove unexpected staged media files.

cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

summary: Windows allowlist execution could use workspace shadows
description:
### Summary

Windows allowlist execution could use workspace shadows. In affected versions, PowerShell command analysis could approve an exact executable from `PATH` but later run a same-named executable from the workspace directory.

This advisory is scoped to Windows hosts using exec allowlist mode with a PowerShell inner command and a workspace-controlled executable sharing the approved basename. It does not rely on replacement of the approved executable itself.

### Impact

If lower-trust content could place an executable in the workspace and steer an approved PowerShell command, OpenClaw could execute the workspace file instead of the allowlisted path. The process would run with the Gateway or node-host user's privileges.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid bare executable names inside approved PowerShell commands and keep executable files out of agent-writable workspaces.

summary: Signal reactions could bind to the wrong approval
description:
### Summary

Signal reactions could bind to the wrong approval. In affected versions, an approval reaction could attach to ordinary outbound text instead of the structured approval request it was intended to resolve.

This advisory is scoped to Signal approval reactions when unrelated outbound messages and a pending approval were present in the same conversation. It does not change the authority of correctly identified approvers.

### Impact

A reaction to unrelated text could be interpreted as approving or denying a pending host action. Practical impact depends on the pending request, conversation timing, and actions available to the OpenClaw process.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid reaction-based approvals in Signal, use another approval surface, and cancel pending requests when unrelated messages appear.

cwes.name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information

summary: chat.send could expose owner-only infrastructure tools
description:
### Summary

`chat.send` could expose owner-only infrastructure tools. In affected versions, a non-owner caller in an identity-bearing Gateway deployment could start a chat turn whose tool inventory included `gateway` and `cron`.

This advisory is scoped to Gateway authentication modes that honor caller identity and narrower operator scopes. Shared-secret token and password callers are full trusted operators under OpenClaw's security model.

### Impact

A write-scoped non-owner caller could cause an agent turn to invoke owner-only configuration or scheduling operations, including persistent state changes. Practical impact depends on the tools selected by the model and the caller's ability to steer the turn.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, restrict `chat.send` to administrators in identity-bearing deployments and remove `gateway` and `cron` from affected agent tool policies.

summary: Config revision hashes could expose password verifiers
description:
### Summary

Redacted configuration responses could include deterministic hashes computed over the original unredacted configuration. When a Gateway password had low entropy and the rest of the configuration was reconstructable, those values acted as offline password verifiers.

### Impact

A caller able to obtain the redacted configuration could test password candidates without reaching the rate-limited Gateway authentication path. Recovering the password could grant the documented shared-secret operator authority. Practical exploitation depended on a weak password and sufficient knowledge of every other hashed configuration value. Secret references were not affected in the same way.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, use a high-entropy Gateway token or password, prefer secret references over inline low-entropy values, and restrict `config.get` to trusted operators.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: Group activation changes could omit owner authorization
description:
### Summary

Group activation changes could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner channel sender could change whether a group required mention-based activation.

This advisory is scoped to persistent `/activation` policy changes. It does not make session presence or conversation ownership a security boundary; the failed control is the documented owner requirement for changing channel trigger policy.

### Impact

A non-owner sender could make the agent respond more broadly in a group or suppress expected activation behavior. This could expose responses to additional group traffic or reduce availability until an owner restored the intended setting.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable activation-setting commands in shared channels and verify group activation configuration after untrusted command activity.

summary: Codex computer-use install could omit owner authorization
description:
### Summary

Codex computer-use install could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner channel sender could install a Codex plugin and cause its configured MCP process to start on the OpenClaw host.

This advisory is scoped to the Codex computer-use installation command. Installed plugins remain trusted code under OpenClaw's security model; the failed boundary is authorization to install that code in the first place.

### Impact

A non-owner sender with command access could install attacker-selected plugin code and execute a host MCP process with the OpenClaw user's privileges. This could affect host confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable Codex computer-use installation in message channels and review installed Codex plugins for unexpected entries.

summary: Workspace endpoint override could expose Azure Speech credentials
description:
### Summary

A workspace endpoint override could expose Azure Speech credentials. In affected versions, an untrusted workspace `.env` could set `AZURE_SPEECH_ENDPOINT` because the workspace filter did not block the `_ENDPOINT` suffix. Azure Speech preferred that value over its configured region.

This advisory is scoped to operators who started OpenClaw in attacker-controlled workspace content, configured Azure Speech with a key and region, and had not set a trusted endpoint override.

### Impact

When Azure Speech made a synthesis or voice-list request, the attacker-selected endpoint received the operator's Azure Speech key in the request header. The exposed key could then be used against the operator's Azure Speech resource.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, run OpenClaw only from trusted workspaces or set `AZURE_SPEECH_ENDPOINT` through a trusted process or global runtime environment.

cwes.name: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere

summary: Claude permission replies could omit owner authorization
description:
### Summary

Claude permission replies could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner channel sender could approve or deny a pending Claude Code permission request through the MCP channel bridge.

This advisory is scoped to Claude permission prompts delivered through configured message channels. It does not change OpenClaw's shared-agent model; the failed boundary is the explicit owner requirement for resolving host permission requests.

### Impact

When a Claude Code run was waiting for permission, a non-owner sender with channel command access could approve an action intended for the owner. Practical impact depends on the pending action and the host capabilities requested by Claude Code.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid delivering Claude permission prompts to channels with non-owner participants and cancel unattended pending requests.

summary: Browser CDP connections could discard DNS pinning
description:
### Summary

Browser CDP connections could discard DNS pinning. In affected versions, OpenClaw validated one DNS result for a configured CDP hostname but raw WebSocket and Playwright transports performed a later independent resolution.

This advisory is scoped to configured remote CDP endpoints. It does not treat intentional local browser control as a vulnerability; the failed boundary was the SSRF policy that approved one destination but connected to another.

### Impact

An attacker who controlled an approved CDP hostname or its DNS answers could use rebinding to make the Gateway connect to a loopback, private, link-local, metadata, or other policy-denied address. Practical impact depended on remote CDP configuration, DNS timing, and services reachable from the Gateway host.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable hostname-based remote CDP endpoints or restrict them to trusted, stable infrastructure.

summary: WhatsApp session resets could bypass command authorization
description:
### Summary

WhatsApp session resets could bypass command authorization. In affected versions, a group sender admitted for ordinary messages could use `/new <model>` to reset the shared group session and persist a provider and model override even when canonical command policy denied that sender.

This advisory is scoped to WhatsApp group senders who pass ordinary message admission but fail `commands.allowFrom` or owner command authorization. The failed boundary is the configured distinction between message admission and command authorization.

### Impact

A command-denied group member could select a provider and model already allowed by the operator for later turns in the shared group session. This could change provider routing, cost, data flow, or availability. It does not add a provider or grant host execution.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, ensure WhatsApp group admission and `commands.allowFrom` contain the same trusted senders, and reset affected group sessions after unauthorized `/new` attempts.

summary: Browser relay authentication could exhaust shared pending capacity
description:
### Summary

The Browser extension relay reserved entries in a single global pending-authentication pool before a client proved possession of the relay key. An unauthenticated network source could hold every pending slot and prevent a paired extension from completing Browser Relay Authentication v2.

### Impact

Operators with a network-reachable Browser relay could experience denial of service for paired Chrome extensions while an attacker maintained enough silent WebSocket upgrades. The issue did not disclose the relay key, browser data, or authenticated relay capability.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.2`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.2` or later. Until upgraded, restrict network access to the Browser extension relay route, avoid exposing it to lower-trust networks, and restart the relay if its pending-authentication capacity becomes saturated.

summary: iOS Control UI did not enforce saved Gateway TLS pins
description:
### Summary

The iOS Control UI did not enforce saved Gateway TLS pins. In affected versions, authenticated Terminal and session Dashboard WebViews omitted the saved Gateway fingerprint even though native connections enforced it.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When an iOS user had accepted a Gateway fingerprint, an attacker who could redirect the same host and port and present a different certificate accepted by iOS system trust could serve a replacement Control UI page. Opening Terminal or a session Dashboard allowed that page to read the injected Gateway token or password. The credential could provide operator access, including reading sensitive Gateway state and invoking host-capable tools.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.11`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade OpenClaw for iOS to `2026.8.11` or later. Before upgrading, avoid the in-app Terminal and session Dashboard for pinned Gateways when network routing or installed certificate authorities are not fully trusted.

summary: Browser proxy could miss its admin scope
description:
### Summary

Browser proxy could miss its admin scope. In affected versions, a write-scoped caller in an identity-bearing Gateway deployment could reach browser control through `node.invoke` even though direct `browser.request` access required administrator scope.

This advisory is scoped to Gateway authentication modes that honor caller identity and narrower operator scopes. Shared-secret token and password callers are full trusted operators under OpenClaw's security model.

### Impact

A write-scoped caller with access to a connected browser-capable node could inspect pages, navigate tabs, or interact with browser-visible applications without the configured admin requirement. Practical impact depends on the browser profile and signed-in state.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, restrict `node.invoke` to administrators in identity-bearing deployments and disconnect sensitive browser nodes.

summary: sessions.create could miss admin scope for keyed reconfiguration
description:
### Summary

`sessions.create` could miss admin scope for keyed reconfiguration. In affected versions, an `operator.write` caller could target an existing session key while supplying model or thinking changes that `sessions.patch` reserved for `operator.admin`.

This advisory is scoped to the Gateway operator-scope boundary. It does not create isolation between mutually untrusted users on one Gateway; it enforces the documented distinction between issued write and admin credentials.

### Impact

A write-scoped operator client could change an existing session's model, provider, thinking level, and configured auth-profile selection. Impact was limited to models and credentials already configured by the operator, but the mutation bypassed the explicit admin gate and could redirect later session traffic.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, do not issue write-only Gateway credentials to clients that can call keyed `sessions.create`.

summary: Agent cron tool could reach operator command jobs
description:
### Summary

Agent cron tool could reach operator command jobs. In affected versions, a model-visible agent caller could read and force-run ownerless command cron jobs routed to the same agent even though command cron was reserved for operator administration.

This advisory is scoped to the model-tool versus operator-admin boundary. It does not claim arbitrary command construction: the affected caller could inspect or replay an existing operator-authored command job.

### Impact

A lower-trust message capable of steering an agent with the cron tool could read a matching command job's stored environment and force-run that job while disabled or before it was due. Practical impact depended on the secrets and commands the operator had placed in existing jobs.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, remove the cron tool from lower-trust agents and avoid storing sensitive environment values in ownerless command jobs.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: Matrix authorization could conflate case-distinct user IDs
description:
### Summary

Matrix authorization lowercased complete user IDs, including historical localparts and the case-sensitive server-name portion. Distinct authenticated Matrix accounts could therefore normalize to the same OpenClaw authorization identity.

### Impact

A Matrix participant with a colliding account identifier could inherit allowlist, owner-command, exec-approval, or plugin-approval authority configured for another account. Exploitation required a protocol-valid pair of identifiers that differed only by characters OpenClaw folded. Display-name matching was not required.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `@openclaw/matrix` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, avoid authorization entries whose complete Matrix IDs differ only by case or Unicode folding, and review configured allowlists and approver identities for possible collisions.

summary: Feishu unpin could miss cross-context policy
description:
### Summary

Feishu unpin could miss cross-context policy. In affected versions, the native `chatId` parameter was not declared as a delivery target, so `unpin` could avoid the shared same-provider target check.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider` was disabled, an admitted sender could remove a pin from another Feishu group that the sender and configured account were otherwise permitted to access. Feishu membership and group authorization still applied, and the demonstrated issue was limited to message mutation policy.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable Feishu pin-management actions for lower-trust senders.

summary: Feishu tools could use disabled default accounts
description:
### Summary

Feishu model tools could select a configured default account without checking whether that account was disabled. In a multi-account setup, an enabled sibling could keep a tool family available while an invocation used the disabled default account's retained credentials.

### Impact

A model tool call could read or modify Feishu resources through an identity the operator intended to revoke. The available actions depended on the disabled app's scopes and enabled tool families. Exploitation required the specific disabled-default and enabled-sibling configuration.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `@openclaw/feishu` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, remove credentials from disabled accounts, change `defaultAccount` to an enabled eligible account, and restart OpenClaw after disabling a Feishu identity.

summary: Exec wrapper allowlists could trust arbitrary inner commands
description:
### Summary

Exec approval policy could trust a command-running wrapper without inspecting the command carried in its arguments. After an operator allowlisted or permanently approved a benign wrapper invocation, a later agent turn could substitute an arbitrary inner command without another prompt.

### Impact

Affected deployments could execute commands with the OpenClaw process's host privileges outside the operator's reviewed approval. Exploitation required the relevant wrapper to resolve on the host and a prior operator decision allowing that wrapper. Transparent shell carriers and opaque utilities such as process monitors or tracing wrappers were affected through related trust-resolution gaps.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, remove standing approvals for command-running wrappers, avoid allowlisting wrapper executables for arbitrary arguments, and require per-invocation approval for commands using shell carriers, monitors, tracers, namespace tools, or proxy wrappers.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

summary: iOS Share Extension stored Gateway credentials outside Keychain
description:
### Summary

The iOS Share Extension stored Gateway credentials outside Keychain. In affected versions, the app stored the Share relay token and password as cleartext JSON in App Group UserDefaults. This created a second credential copy outside the device-bound Keychain storage used elsewhere in the app.

### Affected configurations

This affects iOS installations with a configured Share relay when an attacker obtains an unencrypted Finder/iTunes backup or extracts the App Group container from a jailbroken or forensically imaged device.

### Impact

An attacker with one of these artifacts could recover a still-valid Gateway token or password and authenticate with its operator authority. The issue required prior access to a backup or extracted device container; it did not expose credentials remotely from a healthy device.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched iOS version is `2026.8.11`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade OpenClaw for iOS to `2026.8.11` or later. Before upgrading, avoid unencrypted device backups and rotate Gateway credentials if an affected backup or device image may have left your control.

summary: Channel read actions could skip target allowlists
description:
### Summary

Channel read actions could skip target allowlists. In affected versions, explicit read targets in Microsoft Teams, Feishu, Matrix, and Google Chat could reach channels or rooms outside the configured read policy.

This advisory is scoped to caller-supplied targets for message, reaction, pin, member, and related metadata reads in the named plugins. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model or create per-user isolation within one Gateway.

### Impact

A lower-trust sender or steered agent with access to a channel read action could retrieve content or metadata from a target excluded by the operator's channel allowlist. Practical impact depends on the bot account's platform permissions.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade each affected channel plugin to `2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable explicit-target read actions or limit the connected bot account to allowed channels at the platform level.

summary: Revoked Canvas capability could remain active during disconnect
description:
### Summary

Revoked Canvas capability could remain active during disconnect. In affected versions, node revocation invalidated the WebSocket client but Canvas HTTP authorization continued accepting and renewing its capability until close cleanup finished.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

A revoked paired node could continue using its previously granted Canvas capability during the WebSocket close grace period. Practical impact was limited to the capability's configured routes and the short interval before connection cleanup, but revocation did not take effect at the owner-held invalidation point.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, restart the Gateway after revoking a node with Canvas access.

summary: Webhook TaskFlow cancellation could target unrelated sessions
description:
### Summary

A webhook TaskFlow route could accept and store an arbitrary child session key, then use that key during cancellation without confirming that the child belonged to the route's configured parent session.

### Impact

A holder of one webhook route secret who knew another live child session key could stop unrelated ACP or subagent work outside that route's authority. The demonstrated effect was session cancellation and associated task-state change; it did not grant access to the cancelled session's content.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable webhook TaskFlow cancellation on routes available to lower-trust callers, rotate exposed route secrets, and avoid accepting remote child-session identifiers unless their ownership is independently verified.

summary: Synology pre-auth limits could lock out valid webhooks
description:
### Summary

Synology pre-auth limits could lock out valid webhooks. In affected versions, invalid-token throttling ran before authentication and identified requests by the raw proxy socket address.

### Affected configurations

This affected Synology Chat webhooks behind a trusted reverse proxy or tunnel where multiple external clients shared one socket address at OpenClaw.

### Impact

An unauthenticated sender could consume the shared invalid-token budget and cause later valid Synology Chat callbacks to be rejected until the rate-limit window cleared. The attacker could not obtain a valid token or access message data; impact was temporary channel availability loss.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid placing untrusted traffic and Synology callbacks behind the same proxy source address, or enforce per-client limits at the proxy.

summary: Video asset downloads could reach private destinations
description:
### Summary

Video asset downloads could reach private destinations. In affected versions, the OpenClaw CLI fetched a provider-returned video asset URL without applying the network destination checks used for untrusted remote URLs.

This advisory is scoped to video-generation providers that return a remote asset URL. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

A malicious or compromised provider could return a private or loopback URL after an operator requested video generation, causing the CLI to make a server-side request. Practical impact depends on the services reachable from the OpenClaw host.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable video generation from providers that are not fully trusted.

summary: Structured attachments could hide unvalidated host paths
description:
### Summary

Structured message attachments accepted several equivalent source fields, but sandbox validation stopped after the first populated field. Telegram later processed every populated source, allowing an out-of-sandbox host path to be hidden behind an allowed attachment source.

### Impact

A sandboxed model could cause Telegram delivery to read and send a known host file that OpenClaw's sandbox media policy would reject on its own. Exploitation required a useful host path and an allowed Telegram delivery target. The issue bypassed path validation; it did not provide general filesystem listing.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, deny Telegram attachment actions to sandboxed or lower-trust agents and reject structured attachments containing more than one source field before delivery.

Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize

summary: LINE group allowlist could inherit DM access
description:
### Summary

LINE group allowlist could inherit DM access. In affected versions, an account using `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` without `groupAllowFrom` silently reused the account's DM `allowFrom` values for group admission.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When DM access was broader than intended group access, including open DMs with `allowFrom: ["*"]`, a group participant could trigger the agent despite the configured group allowlist mode. Practical impact depended on the tools and conversation data exposed to that LINE account.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `@openclaw/line@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, set an explicit finite `groupAllowFrom` for every account using group allowlist mode.

summary: OpenShell filesystem mutations could race path validation
description:
### Summary

OpenShell filesystem mutations could race path validation. In affected versions, `remove`, `mkdir`, or `rename` could act on a different filesystem target after OpenClaw completed its sandbox path-safety check.

This advisory is scoped to OpenShell local mirror mutations during a concurrent path change. It does not rely on an operator intentionally granting host filesystem access outside the sandbox.

### Impact

An attacker able to win the filesystem race could cause a sandboxed operation to mutate a host path outside the intended mirror root. Practical impact could include unauthorized deletion, directory creation, or rename operations with the OpenClaw process user's permissions.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable OpenShell filesystem mutation operations for lower-trust workloads and avoid concurrent changes to mirror paths.

summary: Memory tools could retain revoked access
description:
### Summary

Existing `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools could continue using an enabled configuration captured at creation after an operator hot-disabled memory. The execution-time resolver treated explicit disablement like an unavailable snapshot and restored stale authority.

### Impact

During an already-running agent turn, the model could continue searching or reading durable memory after the operator revoked that access. The exposure lasted for the remainder of the affected run and required memory to be disabled while a previously created tool remained active.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, restart active agent runs after disabling memory, and stop or restart the Gateway when immediate revocation is required rather than relying only on hot configuration reload.

summary: Synology file delivery could lose DNS pinning
description:
### Summary

Synology file delivery could lose DNS pinning. In affected versions, the Gateway validated one DNS result for a file URL but passed the original hostname to the NAS, where it could resolve to a different destination.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When Synology Chat attachment delivery accepted a remotely influenced hostname, DNS rebinding could make the NAS fetch a private or otherwise policy-denied resource and return it to the addressed conversation. Practical impact depended on NAS routing, resolver behavior, and the response available at the private destination.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable remote URL attachment forwarding in Synology Chat.

summary: Browser node targets could bypass sandbox host control
description:
### Summary

Browser node targets could bypass sandbox host control. In affected versions, a sandboxed browser tool could select a paired node and reach host browser actions despite `allowHostControl=false`.

This advisory is scoped to sandboxed sessions using the browser tool with a node target. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-node model; the failed boundary is the operator's explicit sandbox decision to deny host control from that session.

### Impact

A lower-trust input able to steer the sandboxed agent could inspect or manipulate a browser on a paired node. Practical impact depends on the connected browser profile, signed-in state, and actions exposed by the browser plugin.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, remove browser tools and paired-node targets from sandboxed agents configured with host control disabled.

summary: Codex bind could omit owner authorization
description:
### Summary

Codex bind could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner channel sender could create a native Codex conversation binding and start host-capable Codex turns.

This advisory is scoped to the Codex plugin's native binding controls. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-plugin model: Codex remains trusted once an owner authorizes its use, while creating or changing a native binding requires owner or administrator authority.

### Impact

A non-owner sender with command access could bind a conversation to the native Codex runtime and reach the files, tools, and processes available to that runtime. Practical impact depends on the configured Codex permissions and host environment.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable Codex bind commands in channels with non-owner participants and remove unintended native bindings.

summary: WhatsApp login tool could reach non-owner turns
description:
### Summary

The WhatsApp login tool could be exposed through the generic channel-tool path without preserving the originating sender's owner status. An admitted non-owner turn could request a forced login and receive a new QR code for a configured account.

### Impact

A non-owner sender able to steer the tool could disconnect or replace the Gateway's WhatsApp account, causing loss of availability and unauthorized account relinking. Successful takeover required scanning the returned QR code with another phone. The issue affected the owner-only tool boundary rather than WhatsApp transport authentication.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `@openclaw/whatsapp` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable the WhatsApp login tool after setup, restrict agent access to owner-controlled conversations, and avoid exposing tool-capable agents to non-owner senders.

summary: Escaped newlines could confuse exec allowlist parsing
description:
### Summary

Escaped newlines could confuse exec allowlist parsing. In affected versions, the command parser could describe and authorize one visible shell word sequence while execution included an additional command hidden by newline parsing.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When exec allowlist or approval policy trusted the parsed command, lower-trust model input could cause an additional command to execute without the expected prompt. Practical impact depended on the exec host, sandbox mode, process permissions, and the commands available to the agent.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable exec for lower-trust agents or require review outside the affected parser path for every command.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

summary: Cron tool could accept mixed-case command payloads
description:
### Summary

Cron tool could accept mixed-case command payloads. In affected versions, a mixed-case payload kind could pass the agent-facing shell-execution guard and later normalize into a command job.

This advisory is scoped to cron jobs created or edited through the model-facing `cron` tool. Direct CLI and authorized Gateway scheduling surfaces remain trusted operator controls.

### Impact

An actor able to steer a tool-enabled agent could create a persistent cron job that executed attacker-selected commands with the OpenClaw process user's privileges. Practical impact includes access to host files, credentials, and scheduled service availability.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, remove the `cron` tool from agents exposed to lower-trust content and inspect scheduled jobs for command payloads.

summary: Trajectory export could omit owner authorization
description:
### Summary

Trajectory export could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner sender in a direct conversation could request, approve, and receive an owner-only trajectory bundle.

This advisory is scoped to `/export-trajectory`, which is documented as an owner command. It does not change the intentionally broader authorization contract of `/export-session` or create per-user isolation within a shared Gateway.

### Impact

A non-owner sender could receive prompts, model messages, tool schemas and results, runtime events, and local path metadata from the affected session. Practical impact depends on the contents recorded in that trajectory.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable trajectory export commands in channels with non-owner participants and remove unexpected exported bundles.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: Microsoft Teams access-group failures could admit unlisted senders
description:
### Summary

Microsoft Teams access-group failures could admit unlisted senders. In affected versions, missing or unsupported configured access groups produced denied results that were not rejected by the final message-admission check.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When `groupPolicy` was set to `allowlist` with an affected access-group entry, an unlisted Teams member could trigger the configured agent despite the administrator's group boundary. Practical impact depended on the conversations, tools, and data available to that agent.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid unresolved access-group entries and use explicit supported sender or conversation allowlists.

summary: File-transfer approvals could widen durable authority
description:
### Summary

File-transfer `allow-always` approvals could preserve more authority than the operator reviewed. Literal path characters could later be interpreted as glob syntax, and node-specific grants could be reused by another node with the same display name.

### Impact

After an operator approved one file-transfer request, a later agent request could reuse that standing grant for a sibling path or a different node that was not shown in the approval. Depending on the original operation, this could broaden durable read or write access. Exploitation still required a prior operator approval and a matching widened target.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, avoid `allow-always` for file-transfer requests containing glob metacharacters and use unique node display names. Remove and recreate existing standing file-transfer grants after upgrading.

summary: Skill tool dispatch could skip owner-only policy
description:
### Summary

Skill tool dispatch could skip owner-only policy. In affected versions, an allowlisted non-owner invoking a skill-backed command could reach owner-only tools because the dispatch path did not carry the sender's owner status or apply the owner-only tool filter.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

A non-owner sender authorized to invoke the affected skill command could access tools backed by server credentials and capabilities that OpenClaw reserves for owners. Practical impact depended on which owner-only command tool the installed skill exposed.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable skill tool dispatch for non-owner senders and audit skills that map commands to owner-only tools.

summary: Reusable exec approvals could authorize changed arguments
description:
### Summary

Reusable exec approvals could authorize changed arguments. In affected versions on macOS and Linux, selecting Allow Always for one exact command persisted a path-only grant. Later uses of the same executable with different arguments could therefore run without a new prompt.

This advisory is scoped to generated Allow Always entries. It does not treat operator-authored path-only allowlist rules as exact-argument grants; the failed boundary was OpenClaw broadening an exact command approved by the operator when it persisted that grant.

### Impact

After an operator approved a benign command, later untrusted content that influenced the agent could reuse its executable with different target or output arguments. Depending on the tool, this could send local files, overwrite user-writable files, or reach internal services without showing another approval prompt. Exploitation requires a prior persistent approval for the same executable.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, use one-time approval for commands whose arguments select network targets, input files, or output paths, and remove generated broad Allow Always entries.

summary: Trusted-host DNS checks could admit unspecified addresses
description:
### Summary

Trusted-host DNS checks could admit unspecified addresses. In affected versions, a trusted hostname that resolved to `0.0.0.0` or `::` could connect to a loopback service despite OpenClaw's SSRF destination checks.

This advisory is scoped to fetches that use the trusted-host DNS recheck. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When an attacker could influence DNS for an allowed hostname, a guarded fetch could reach a service bound only to loopback and disclose its response. Practical impact depends on the reachable service and the data it returns.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid trusting hostnames whose DNS answers are outside the operator's control.

summary: Truncated tar listings could bypass extraction limits
description:
### Summary

The `tar.bz2` skill installer treated bounded command-output suffixes as complete archive listings. A crafted archive could push prohibited entries out of both retained listings, pass entry and size checks, and then be extracted in full.

### Impact

After an operator approved installation of a malicious or compromised skill archive, over-limit files or entry counts could be persisted in the skill tools directory and consume disk space or inodes. The demonstrated issue bypassed OpenClaw's explicit extraction budgets; it did not execute archive contents by itself.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, avoid installing `.tar.bz2` or `.tbz2` skills from untrusted sources and inspect or extract such archives with an independently bounded tool before installation.

summary: Embedding fallback could forward a provider key across vendors
description:
### Summary

Embedding fallback could forward a provider key across vendors. In affected versions, memory embedding failover could reuse the primary provider's configured API key while sending the request to a different fallback provider.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When remote embedding fallback was configured and the primary provider failed, a credential intended for one vendor could be sent as a bearer token to another vendor. Practical impact depended on the configured providers, whether failover occurred, and the privileges attached to the primary provider key.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable cross-provider embedding fallback or configure providers with separate narrowly scoped credentials.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: Dreaming could widen restricted sender authority
description:
### Summary

Session-derived memory could lose the originating requester's restrictions before later dreaming runs processed it. Text from an admitted sender with limited tools could be persisted without its untrusted provenance, then supplied to an unattended agent with broader file and command capabilities.

### Impact

In deployments with session-memory capture and dreaming enabled, a restricted external sender could place instructions that a later background model might follow with authority unavailable to the original turn. Successful exploitation required the content to be captured, selected for later processing, and followed by the model. Resulting actions could affect files, commands, or services available to the dreaming agent.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable dreaming for agents that accept restricted external senders, disable session-memory capture for those conversations, or run background memory processing without mutation and command tools.

summary: Discord realtime transcripts could inherit another speaker's owner status
description:
### Summary

Discord realtime transcripts could inherit another speaker's owner status. In affected versions, concurrent control-classified voice transcripts could consume speaker context belonging to another participant after an asynchronous control check.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

In Discord `agent-proxy` voice sessions using the affected realtime control path, a non-owner utterance could reach the downstream agent boundary marked as owner. This could apply owner-sensitive behavior to the wrong speaker. Practical impact depended on concurrent transcript timing and the tools and commands available to that agent.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.9.2`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.9.2` or later. Before upgrading, disable Discord realtime voice for agents that distinguish owner and non-owner senders.

cwes.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

summary: Unicode fallback could escape workspaceOnly roots
description:
### Summary

When `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` was enabled, Unicode filename fallback could normalize already-validated parent directory components. On filesystems where canonically equivalent sibling directories coexist, a missing path inside the workspace could be retried against a sibling outside it.

### Impact

An admitted requester could cause a tool-enabled agent to read a known file outside its configured workspace boundary. Exploitation required a filesystem layout with distinct canonically equivalent parent directory names and knowledge of a useful target path. It did not rely on symlinks or hardlinks.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, avoid workspace paths with canonically equivalent Unicode sibling names and deny filesystem read tools to lower-trust senders on affected hosts.

Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize

summary: Workspace Cloud SDK arguments could execute code during Gmail setup
description:
### Summary

Workspace Cloud SDK arguments could execute code during Gmail setup. In affected versions, an untrusted workspace `.env` could set `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_ARGS`. Gmail setup inherited that value when starting `gcloud`, whose launcher passed it as arguments to Python.

This advisory is scoped to operators who started OpenClaw in attacker-controlled workspace content and then invoked the Gmail setup flow.

### Impact

A crafted `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_ARGS` value could make the trusted Python interpreter execute attacker-supplied code when Gmail setup ran `gcloud`. The code ran with the OpenClaw host user's permissions and could read credentials, modify files, or start other processes.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, run Gmail setup only from trusted workspaces and clear inherited `CLOUDSDK_*` variables before invoking it.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

summary: MCP loopback could omit sandbox tool deny policy
description:
### Summary

MCP loopback could omit sandbox tool deny policy. In affected versions, a sandboxed coding-agent session could list and invoke tools explicitly denied by `sandbox.tools.deny`.

This advisory is scoped to the bundled MCP loopback used by sandboxed coding-agent sessions. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When MCP loopback is enabled for a sandboxed session, the session could reach a denied tool and access data or actions that the operator intended to exclude. Practical impact depends on the denied tools and their granted capabilities.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, disable MCP loopback for sandboxed coding agents or remove sensitive tools from the Gateway inventory.

summary: iOS deep-link logs could expose unattended credentials
description:
### Summary

OpenClaw for iOS logged the complete unattended-agent deep-link URL as public diagnostic data. The URL could contain a persistent bearer key together with message and delivery parameters, leaving the credential available in copied unified logs or diagnostic archives.

### Impact

A party that obtained affected logs could reuse an unrotated key in a forged deep link to submit attacker-chosen agent requests without the normal local confirmation. Exploitation also required a legitimate keyed link to have been processed and a way to invoke the custom URL scheme on the connected device. Invalid or absent keys still required confirmation.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.11`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade OpenClaw for iOS to `2026.8.11` or later. Rotate unattended deep-link keys that may appear in affected diagnostics, remove retained diagnostic archives containing those links, and avoid sharing device logs from affected versions.

cwes.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

summary: Talk Voice changes could omit admin authorization
description:
### Summary

Talk Voice changes could omit admin authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner external-channel sender could use `/voice set` to persist the Gateway's configured Talk voice.

This advisory is scoped to the mutating Talk Voice command. Read-only voice status remains available according to normal channel policy, while persistent Gateway configuration changes require owner or administrator authority.

### Impact

A non-owner sender with command access could change the voice used by Talk responses for the configured provider. This affects configuration integrity and future voice output but does not by itself expose credentials or grant additional host capabilities.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable `/voice set` in external channels or limit channel command access to owners.

summary: Session filename generation could regain denied tools
description:
### Summary

Session filename generation could regain denied tools. In affected versions, session-memory filename generation created an embedded helper with tools that the originating sender's policy had removed.

This advisory is scoped to the named feature and configuration. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When session-memory filename generation was enabled for an agent reachable by lower-trust senders, model-mediated instructions could invoke tools outside that sender's effective policy. Demonstrated impact included creating persistent scheduled work. Practical impact depended on the model following the injected instruction and on which tools the helper exposed.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable session-memory filename generation for agents reachable by lower-trust senders.

summary: Slack group DMs could skip sender allowlists
description:
### Summary

Slack group DMs could skip sender allowlists. In affected versions, a sender in a multi-person direct message could trigger an OpenClaw agent even when the configured Slack group sender policy did not allow that sender.

This advisory is scoped to Slack multi-person direct messages and their message, command, and interaction ingress. It does not change OpenClaw's trusted-operator model: authenticated Gateway operators, installed plugins, and intentional local execution surfaces remain trusted unless a separate policy, approval, allowlist, sandbox, or auth boundary is crossed.

### Impact

When a Slack agent was present in a group DM, a disallowed participant could trigger the agent within the tools and data already granted to that agent. Practical impact depends on the agent's tool policy and channel configuration.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `@openclaw/slack@2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, do not add tool-enabled agents to multi-person direct messages containing untrusted participants.

summary: message.action could trust spoofed requester provenance
description:
### Summary

`message.action` could trust spoofed requester provenance. In affected versions, a write-scoped caller in an identity-bearing Gateway deployment could supply another sender's identifier to channel authorization checks.

This advisory is scoped to Gateway authentication modes that honor caller identity and narrower operator scopes. Shared-secret token and password callers are full trusted operators under OpenClaw's security model.

### Impact
